mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in total non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates strong labor market conditions that support corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where PAYEMS rises by at least 0.5% in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: CPIAUCSL exceeding 255 signals elevated inflationary pressures that trigger central bank tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL exceeds 255.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent increases in FEDFUNDS and UNRATE signal monetary tightening combined with labor market deterioration, typically causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where both FEDFUNDS and UNRATE rise by at least 0.1% in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion regimes, rising housing starts (HOUST) indicate robust consumer demand for housing, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances during late-cycle expansion when HOUST rises by at least 0.5% in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) reflects strong manufacturing output, supporting corporate profit growth and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO rises by at least 0.5% in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: UNRATE exceeding 4.0% signals significant labor market weakness that triggers risk-off sentiment, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 4.0.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in GDP (GDPC1) and industrial production (INDPRO) indicate synchronized economic demand and supply expansion, typically resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where both GDPC1 and INDPRO rise by at least 0.5% in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: In monetary tightening cycles, rising FEDFUNDS signals reduced liquidity and higher discount rates, typically causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances during monetary tightening cycles when FEDFUNDS rises by at least 0.1% in the prior month.
